statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail crosses into the elevated band at 27% on observed post-open continuation and a failed retracement, while Stress stays extreme at 83%.
recommendation: Tail is above the block threshold, so the mapped state is BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES rather than a stronger block. The flagged window is kept narrow, covering the observed continuation phase through the 15:30Z European close, because a reclaim of the session midpoint near 30,712 would invalidate the structure that produced this mapping. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 loses its Globex retracement and prints new session lows after the U.S. cash open, lifting Tail into the block band while Nvidia's buyback and a decaying energy impulse cap the damage
body:
The structural picture changed inside the last hour. NQ futures traded as high as 30,920.75 in Globex after Friday's 30,889.25 settlement, sold to 30,531.00, and the roughly 42% retracement to 30,694.75 reported in the 13:00Z assessment has now failed: the session low was extended to 30,504.00 and price is near 30,573.75, about 17% of the session range above the low. Three independent reads inside the 14:18Z-14:31Z window agree. Cash ^NDX is 30,288.41, down 1.04% against a 30,608.13 previous close with a 30,234.06-30,480.40 range, and QQQ is $736.17, down 1.12%, sitting 14% off its low. That is observed opening-auction continuation with a failed retracement and price holding near the session extreme, which is the specific evidence the 13:00Z publication named as the first genuine sign of mean-reversion failure. It is the reason Tail crosses the block threshold to 27%.

The cross-asset backdrop is aligned on the rates and energy side. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.23% after touching its highest level since 15 June 2007, and the 30-year is near 5.49%, the highest since 2004. WTI is $94.14, up 1.87%, and Brent is $106.48, up 2.07%, after President Trump rejected Tehran's conditional seven-day ceasefire proposal over the weekend. Semiconductors are underperforming, with SMH down 1.30% to $598.69 and AMD and Micron down roughly 3% and 2%. VIX is 15.89, up 6.85% from a 14.87 close.

Three things argue against a higher reading. Nvidia, the largest index weight, is up 2.79% after its board authorised an additional $150 billion of repurchases, taking the remaining programme to $235 billion, so the decline is being carried by the non-Nvidia complex rather than by one-way index liquidation. Gold is down 3.51% to $4,169.70, which is a haven premium unwinding rather than a geopolitical discontinuity, and Brent has already pared from a session high near $108.83 as Saudi East-West pipeline shipments resumed and negotiations are expected to resume this week. Absolute implied volatility near 16 is not pricing a pathological path, and the index decline is only about 1.1%. Stress therefore eases one point to 83% while Tail rises: the environment remains difficult through quarter-end, with unusually wide single-name dispersion, but the magnitude channel is decaying even as the observed path deteriorates. Shared Finviz context was read and rejected as evidence: it was collected at 05:58Z, roughly eight and a half hours stale against the 90-minute freshness limit, with its calendar and futures sections unavailable. All conclusions above rest on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The published Claude series spent the first half of this window in a quiet regime and then repriced. Tail was 8% in the 14:00Z slot on 27 September, drifted to 14% by 23:00Z as the weekend Iran headlines developed, and stepped to 21-24% through the Asian and European sessions on 28 September as crude gapped higher and the long end extended. It peaked at 26% in the 09:00Z hour, the window's only orange print, then eased to 24%, 21% and 22% while the decline retraced and the dominant mode rotated from trend-down to mixed. Stress rose almost monotonically from 66% to a peak of 85%, and Confidence improved from 75% to 87% as live evidence accumulated. All 24 slots are available; none has been revised with hindsight.
outlookSummary: The path starts from observed rather than assumed structure. Conditional Tail is held at 27% for the current hour and the 15:00Z hour, covering the observed continuation phase and the 15:30Z European cash close, then stepped back to the 25% block boundary at 16:00Z and into the watch band from 17:00Z on the assumption that directional efficiency decays once European books close and two-way discovery resumes. Small lifts are carried into the 19:00Z and 20:00Z hours for the power hour, the cash close and quarter-end rebalancing flow two sessions before 30 September. Conditional Tail then falls into the low band from 22:00Z through the Asian session, bottoming at 15%, before rebuilding through the European handover to 20-22% and finishing at 23% for the final slot, which contains the 13:00Z S&P/Case-Shiller release and the 13:30Z U.S. cash open on 29 September. Stress decays from 83% to 73% overnight and rebuilds to 79% on the approach to the 30 September PCE and GDP block. Every slot beyond the current hour is conditional; no future price structure is asserted as observed.
